ਸੰਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਰੇਣੁਕਾ ਲੈ ਮਾਥੈ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ:
The seeker prays to receive the dust of the feet of the holy ones and apply it to the forehead, declaring this sacred ash the true treasure and all accomplishments of life. The act of touching the forehead with the dust of the feet of the sant (the company of the devout) signifies total surrender, the acceptance of humility as the highest spiritual wealth, and the recognition that refuge at the feet of the holy is the only true attainment. The forehead mark publicly declares where one has sought shelter.

Themes: dust of saints' feet, surrender and refuge, humility as treasure, applying to forehead, holy sangat, spiritual wealth, devotion, sacred ash.
ਗੁਰਸਿਖਾਂ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਧੂੜਿ ਦੇਹਿ ਹਮ ਪਾਪੀ ਭੀ ਗਤਿ:
The speaker pleads for the dust beneath the feet of the Guru's Sikhs, seeking the lowest position at the devotees' feet as the path to the highest spiritual state. Acknowledging being a sinner and entangled in vice, the speaker nevertheless hopes for liberation through contact with the holy congregation, sangat. The dust represents both concrete humility and the transformative power of association with the devout, which elevates even the fallen. Salvation flows through surrender to those who themselves walk the path of divine remembrance.

Themes: humility, dust of devotees' feet, liberation of sinners, sangat (company of the devout), grace through association, surrender, spiritual elevation, refuge
ਕਰਉ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਭਗਤ ਜਨ ਧੂਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੩॥:
The speaker offers prostrate reverence to bhagat jan (devout devotees) and presses the dust of their feet to the face — an act of utter self-abasement before those who walk the divine path. The teeka clarifies the deeper longing: to join the sangat (company of the devout) where saints perform bhakti (loving devotion) and together sing the Divine's praises. This is not mere ritual humility but a plea for participation in collective worship, seeking the transformative association of holy persons whose feet carry the fragrance of naam (the divine Name). The gesture of applying foot-dust to the face declares that the devotee's remnants are more precious than personal purity, and that salvation flows through contact with those absorbed in simran (loving remembrance).

Themes: devotee dust on face, prostration before saints, longing for sangat, self-abasement, bhakti participation, holy company, foot-dust as blessing, collective worship
ਟਹਲ ਕਰਉ ਤੇਰੇ ਦਾਸ ਕੀ ਪਗ ਝਾਰਉ ਬਾਲ ॥:
The speaker expresses an uttermost devotion by seeking to serve not the Divine directly, but the Divine's servant—finding God through serving the devotee. Wiping feet with hair is an ancient gesture of complete humility and self-abasement, and the speaker embraces this lowly role with joy. The path to the Divine runs through the sangat (company of the devout); serving God's beloved is the highest form of worship. This is a declaration of where true merit lies.

Themes: service to the devotee, humility and self-abasement, finding God through the sangat, devotion to the Divine's servant, charan kamal (lotus feet), wiping feet with hair, servant of God's servant, supreme love.
ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਧੂਰਿ ਦੇਹੁ ਸੰਤਨ ਕੀ ਸੁਖੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ ਇ:
The seeker pleads for divine compassion to receive the dust of saints' feet, expressing complete humility and desperate longing for spiritual refuge. This is a prayer of surrender, acknowledging that true peace comes only through contact with the holy congregation, sangat. The speaker asks for nothing else—no worldly comfort, only the blessed residue of the devout. Applying this sacred dust to the forehead represents taking shelter at the feet of the awakened ones, the ultimate act of devotion and the sole path to lasting tranquility.

Themes: prayer, saints' dust, divine grace, humility, spiritual longing, refuge, peace, sangat
ਸੰਤਹ ਚਰਣ ਹਮਾਰੋ ਮਾਥਾ ਨੈਨ ਦਰਸੁ ਤਨਿ ਧੂਰਿ ਪਰ:
This is a fervent prayer expressing complete humility and longing for association with holy beings. The speaker seeks to bow their head at the feet of saints, to have their eyes perpetually filled with the sacred sight of the devout, and to have their body covered in the dust of holy feet—an image of total surrender and the highest blessing. The request positions the sangat (company of the devout) as the supreme refuge and the path to spiritual purification.

Themes: devotion to saints, humility and surrender, longing for darshan (sacred vision), dust of holy feet, sangat as refuge, prayer for spiritual union, service to the holy, submission of body and mind.
ਅਤਿ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਮਨਮੋਹਨ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਸਭਹੂ ਮਧਿ ਨਿਰਾਰੇ ॥:
The devotee addresses the Divine with intimate affection, captivated by a beauty that entices the mind and heart. God is present within all creation yet remains fundamentally distinct, set apart from the ordinary. This is a statement of loving wonder at the paradox of immanence and transcendence, where the Beloved enchants the soul while dwelling uniquely amidst the many.

Themes: divine beauty, mind's enchantment, immanence and transcendence, intimate address, loving devotion, distinctiveness of God, captivation of heart, paradox of presence.
ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਰੂਪੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਅਤਿ ਰੰਗ ਰੂੜੋ ਮੇ:
The devotee exclaims in direct address that the divine Name, the divine form, and the divine love are each beautiful, lovely, and pleasing. This is a pausa, a refrain meant for repetition, establishing an aesthetic and emotional stance of wonder and delight in the Lord's attributes. The speaker names the beauty of the Name, the beauty of the form, and the intense beauty of the love as the ground of devotion and the reason for attraction to the Beloved.

Themes: divine beauty, loving praise, aesthetic wonder, naam (the divine Name), divine form, devotional love, repetition as contemplation, direct address to the Lord.
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਰਸਾਲ ਤੂ ॥੧॥:
The Divine is addressed directly as beautiful, the primal source from which all essences and delights flow. This is intimate praise that recognises the Creator as both aesthetically radiant and the wellspring of every rasa—every flavour of experience and spiritual bliss. The speaker declares the Beloved's attractiveness and overflowing fullness, establishing a relationship of devotion and wonder at the One who is the origin of all sweetness and satisfaction.

Themes: divine beauty, source of nectar, rasa, intimate address, praise, devotion, wellspring of bliss, aesthetic wonder.
ਨੈਣ ਪਸੰਦੋ ਸੋਇ ਪੇਖਿ ਮੁਸਤਾਕ ਭਈ ॥:
The Divine is exquisitely pleasing to the eyes; seeing that form, the soul becomes utterly intoxicated and captivated. The vision of the Beloved acts as a potent enchantment, seizing the heart and inducing a state of spiritual rapture. Gazing upon the sacred presence yields an overwhelming infatuation, binding the seeker in ecstatic absorption.

Themes: divine beauty, spiritual intoxication, captivated gaze, ecstatic rapture, vision of the Beloved, loving enchantment, soul's infatuation
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਸੋਭਾ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਦਇਆਲ ਕੀ ਅਪਰ ਅਪਾਰਾ ਰ:
The beautiful glory and radiance of the merciful Lord, the beloved sustainer of the world, spreads forth without any boundary or limit. This is a declaration of praise celebrating the infinite splendor of the compassionate Divine, whose fame is exquisitely lovely and utterly beyond measure. The subject is the magnificence of the Master of the world, described as both captivating in its beauty and immeasurable in its extent, emphasizing divine grace and boundlessness.

Themes: divine glory, infinite splendor, compassionate Lord, Gopal, beloved Master, boundless praise, divine beauty, mercy.
ਅਪੁਨੇ ਸੇਵਕ ਕੀ ਆਪੇ ਰਾਖੈ ਆਪੇ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵੈ ॥:
The Divine personally safeguards the honour and dignity of those who serve, and personally inspires their loving remembrance. Protection and the impulse toward devotion both originate from the One, not from human effort. The devotee's security is guaranteed by divine initiative, and the very act of chanting the divine Name is something the Eternal causes to happen. Grace both shields and moves the servant toward praise.

Themes: divine protection of devotees, naam (the divine Name) as divine gift, simran (loving remembrance) inspired by grace, honour preserved by the Eternal, surrender of personal effort, devotee's dependence on divine initiative
ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ ਰਾਖੈ ਜੁਗਿ ਜੁਗਿ ਰਖਦਾ ਆ:
The Divine protects the honor and dignity of devotees, preserving their reputation and spiritual standing across all ages and eras. This is an eternal pattern: the Lord has consistently guarded those who surrender to him, shielding them from disgrace through every yug (cosmic age). The statement offers reassurance that divine protection is not momentary but historically proven, a perpetual safeguard for the faithful across time.

Themes: divine protection, honor of devotees, eternal constancy, faithfulness across ages, divine-devotee relationship, safeguarding dignity, historical witness, reassurance of divine care
ਭਗਤ ਤੇਰੇ ਸਭਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਣਪਤਿ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ ਤੂੰ ਭਗਤਨ ਕਾ:
The devotee addresses the Divine as Lord of life and Beloved, establishing a mutual bond of love. All bhagats (devotees) hold the Creator dear, and the Creator cherishes the bhagats in return. The statement affirms that devotion is answered with divine affection. The relationship is not one-sided; the Master of breath finds the faithful beloved, just as they find Him. This is a declaration of reciprocal love between the worshipper and the worshipped.

Themes: divine love, bhagat (devotee), pranapati (Lord of life), preetam (Beloved), reciprocal devotion, Lord of breath, divine affection, mutual relationship.
ਭਗਤਾ ਕੀ ਟੇਕ ਤੂੰ ਸੰਤਾ ਕੀ ਓਟ ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਸਿਰਜਨ:
The eternal Creator is the sole refuge and foundation for devotees, the protective shelter for saints. The teeka specifies that it is the divine Name that serves as this support and sanctuary — the Name is the prop on which bhagats (devotees) lean and the fortress shielding sants (holy ones). Declaring the Truth-creating Lord as the only reliable anchor, the refrain affirms that those who seek shelter in the Name find unshakable ground. The faithful rest their weight entirely on that one support, finding safety under divine protection rather than any worldly stay.

Themes: divine refuge, naam as support, shelter of saints, true Creator, devotees' foundation, surrender to the Name, protection of the faithful, eternal sustainer
ਹਰਿ ਜੁਗੁ ਜੁਗੁ ਭਗਤ ਉਪਾਇਆ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਦਾ ਆਇਆ ਰਾਮ:
The Divine sovereign has, age after age, brought devotees into being and unfailingly guarded their dignity. Across every cosmic cycle, the Lord King raises up bhagats (devotees) and shields their honour when the world presses in. This is a declaration of the eternal pattern of divine protection: the Supreme One continuously births lovers of truth and preserves their prestige through every era, ensuring that those who surrender to naam (the divine Name) are never abandoned to disgrace. The stance is one of confident reassurance, affirming that the Protector of the devout has always acted this way and will not stop.

Themes: divine sovereignty, devotee creation across ages, honour preservation, eternal protection pattern, bhagat dignity, cosmic cycles, Lord King, divine faithfulness
ਹਮਰੇ ਕਰਮ ਨ ਬਿਚਰਹੁ ਠਾਕੁਰ ਤੁਮ੍ਹ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਹੁ ਅ:
The devotee pleads with the Divine Master to disregard past actions and the accumulated weight of karma, confessing moral inadequacy while seeking shelter. The request is not for earned reward but for unearned grace, asking God to protect the reputation and dignity of a servant who has no other recourse. The stance is one of desperate humility, entrusting one's honor entirely to the Lord's discretion rather than to one's own record. The teeka emphasizes that the Divine himself must preserve the servant's status, making preservation an act of divine ownership rather than human merit.

Themes: plea for forgiveness, karma and divine grace, honor of the devotee, refuge in the Master, divine compassion over merit, servant-master relationship, surrender of ego, protection of reputation.
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਨਿਤ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਕਰੇ ਕਬੂਲੁ ॥:
The seeker adopts the posture of a beggar asking alms, but the only wealth sought is naam, the divine Name, requested continuously from the Divine Master who accepts and grants the prayer. This image of spiritual poverty and dependence declares that approaching the Creator with humble neediness, asking for nothing but devotion itself, ensures the request is approved. The Lord responds to those who make remembrance their sole petition.

Themes: beggar, divine Name, acceptance of prayer, humility, spiritual petition, Lord as Master, continuous asking, devotion as wealth
ਦੇਹਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਸੰਤੋਖੀਆ ਉਤਰੈ ਮਨ ਕੀ ਭੁਖ ॥:
A direct plea to the Divine for the gift of naam, seeking not worldly provision but the arrival of contentment itself. The speaker asks that the deep restlessness and craving of the mind be finally stilled, with the divine Name as the only food that satisfies. The request positions spiritual satiation as the remedy for the mind's chronic hunger, ending the endless thirst for maya through surrender to divine grace.

Themes: naam, contentment, mental hunger, divine gift, spiritual satisfaction, surrender, santokh, ending craving
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਜਾਚੈ ॥:
The seeker identifies as a spiritual beggar whose only petition is naam (the divine Name), repeating the act of begging again and again before the Lord who is the refuge, master, and giver of all comforts. This is a stance of utter dependence and relentless supplication, declaring that the sole worthy request is for divine remembrance itself. The repeated begging signifies that the soul's asking never ceases, that grace is the only currency, and that the devotee desires nothing except continuous communion with the Divine.

Themes: naam as sole begging request, spiritual beggar posture, relentless supplication, divine refuge and dependence, repeated asking for grace, surrender through asking, Lord as sole provider
ਕਰਹੁ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਗੋਬਿਦੇ ਅਪਨਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵਹ:
A direct plea to the Divine as protector and sustainer of the world — addressed as Gopal, the cowherd who tends all souls, and Gobind, master of creation — asking not for worldly relief but for the grace to be made to chant the divine Name. The petitioner acknowledges that even the act of naam (divine Name) remembrance depends on divine initiative; the Lord must Himself cause the devotee to utter it. This is surrender that recognises its own helplessness: liberation begins not with human effort but with the Creator's compassion activating devotion. The repeated cry for mercy positions simran (loving remembrance) as a gift bestowed, not a practice self-generated.

Themes: plea for divine grace, naam as divine gift, surrender and helplessness, Gopal Gobind as protector-sustainer, dependence on divine initiative, simran activated by compassion, refuge in the Lord
ਜਾਚਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਦੇਹਿ ਪਿਆਰਿਆ ॥:
A destitute seeker addresses the Divine with intimate familiarity, confessing complete dependence and requesting the gift of spiritual welfare. The speaker identifies as a beggar—one who possesses nothing and relies entirely on the Lord's generosity—asking not for worldly goods but for the ultimate good found through the eternal Word. The tone balances desperation with loving closeness, positioning the devotee in humble supplication while claiming a relationship of beloved and lover.

Themes: beggar, divine gift, supplication, spiritual welfare, dependence on God, intimate address, humble request, relationship with the Divine.
ਦਰਿ ਮੰਗਤੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਦੀਜੈ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕਰਿ:
The speaker positions themselves as a beggar at the Divine door, adopting the stance of utter humility and dependence. This is a plea for grace, not a claim of merit—the seeker approaches as one who has nothing and asks for everything. The image of begging conveys spiritual poverty recognized and brought to the only source that can fill it. The request for charity is a request for the gift of naam, for the grace that transforms emptiness into fullness.

Themes: begging at the divine door, plea for grace, spiritual humility, dependence on the Creator, seeking divine charity, mercy as the ultimate gift, surrender, the devotee's poverty.
ਮਉਲਿਓ ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਹੋਇਓ ਹਰਿਆ ਏਕ ਬੂੰਦ ਜਿਨਿ ਪਾਈ:
The mind blossoms open and the body becomes green with spiritual vitality when even a single drop of the divine Name is obtained. The imagery of blooming and verdure signals inner awakening and flourishing that comes from contact with sacred water. External prosperity is not the fruit; the soul itself comes alive, refreshed and expansive, through the smallest taste of divine grace. One drop of amrit (immortal nectar) transforms the whole being.

Themes: spiritual awakening, divine grace, inner transformation, naam (the divine Name), flourishing of the soul, amrit (immortal nectar), mind-body renewal, smallest grace yielding greatest fruit.
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਤ ਸਦ ਹੀ ਰਾਤਾ ॥:
The one who drinks the divine nectar of naam (the divine Name) remains permanently saturated with its colour, forever dyed in deep devotion. The image of drinking captures internal absorption, while being dyed expresses total transformation—every part of the self permeated by love for the Divine. This is not momentary taste but lasting immersion, where the seeker is continuously steeped in God's essence. The state described is one of permanent spiritual intoxication and unshakeable connection.

Themes: divine nectar, spiritual intoxication, naam simran (loving remembrance), inner transformation, permanent devotion, absorption in God, being dyed in divine love, nectar of the Name
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਰਸੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਅਹਿਨਿਸਿ ਪੂਰਨ:
The instruction directs the seeker to sing kirtan (devotional praise) as the essential taste that gives spiritual life, the nectar-essence that sustains the soul. This singing is not occasional but continuous practice. The result is an inner resonance, a celestial sound-current that vibrates within day and night without ceasing. The verse presents sacred music as both the method and the reward: the act of praising the Divine opens an inner channel of bliss that plays perpetually within the heart, transforming consciousness into an instrument of divine sound.

Themes: kirtan as spiritual nectar, inner celestial music, continuous devotional practice, divine sound-current, bliss through praise, naam simran, heart as instrument, unbroken awareness.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸਨਾ ਪੀਉ ਪਿਆਰੀ ॥:
The speaker addresses the tongue as a beloved companion, urging it to drink the amrit (immortal nectar) of naam (the divine Name). This is an exhortation to one's own faculties rather than a philosophical statement, treating the tongue as an agent capable of choosing what it consumes. The nectar represents spiritual sustenance that gives life to the soul, contrasting with ordinary taste. The instruction frames loving remembrance as a voluntary act of drinking, making spiritual practice an intimate act of consumption rather than external ritual.

Themes: divine nectar, tongue as agent, exhortation to self, naam as sustenance, spiritual thirst, voluntary remembrance, soul's nourishment, intimate address.
ਤੇਰਾ ਜਨੁ ਰਾਮ ਰਸਾਇਣਿ ਮਾਤਾ ॥:
The devotee addressed as a humble servant of the Divine is described as being completely intoxicated and absorbed in the rasa (spiritual essence) of the Lord's Name. The imagery of intoxication conveys a state of spiritual ecstasy and detachment from worldly concerns, where the devotee is wholly consumed by loving devotion and inner bliss rather than ordinary consciousness.

Themes: spiritual intoxication, devotee as servant, divine essence, loving absorption, naam (divine Name), spiritual ecstasy, devotional surrender, inner bliss.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਆ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੀ ਹਮ ਨਾਮ ਵਿਟਹੁ ਕ:
Through the Guru's shabad (divine teaching), the seeker drinks the immortal nectar of naam (the divine Name), the essence that grants spiritual life. The act of tasting this divine ambrosia transforms the inner being, and the response is total self-offering — a sacrifice unto the Name itself. The devotee declares utter dedication, willing to be consumed in devotion to that sacred essence. The Word of the Guru is the vessel; the Name is the sweetness; surrender is the result. Drinking the nectar of remembrance is not metaphor alone but the lived experience of absorption in the Divine, producing a state where one's very existence becomes an offering.

Themes: naam as immortal nectar, gur-shabad as means of tasting divine essence, self-sacrifice in devotion, spiritual life through remembrance, surrender to the Name, ambrosial experience of simran (loving remembrance)
ਰਸੁ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਰਸੁ ਅਤਿ ਭਲਾ ਕਿਤੁ ਬਿਧਿ:
The divine Name is described as the supreme essence, a life-giving nectar that surpasses all other flavors. The speaker asks a searching question about obtaining this spiritual sustenance, yearning to consume and internalize the taste of the divine. The longing expresses both the recognition of the Name's supreme value and the seeker's helplessness to attain it through their own efforts. The verse positions the Name as the ultimate source of spiritual vitality.

Themes: divine Name, spiritual nectar, longing for God, supreme essence, inner nourishment, seeker's question, grace versus effort, tasting the divine.
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
An imperative call urging spiritual companions to take shelter in the complete Guru and practice constant remembrance of the divine Name. The image of drinking captures absorbing the essence of the Divine, conveying that true fulfillment comes through internalizing God's presence rather than external pursuits. This is an exhortation to seek refuge in the Guru and commit to naam (the divine Name) as the path to spiritual nourishment.

Themes: divine essence, naam simran (loving remembrance), Guru's shelter, spiritual nourishment, fellowship, imperative instruction, devotion, inner fulfillment
ਬਿਖੈ ਬਨੁ ਫੀਕਾ ਤਿਆਗਿ ਰੀ ਸਖੀਏ ਨਾਮੁ ਮਹਾ ਰਸੁ:
A direct address to the soul as a female companion, urging abandonment of worldly temptations and sensual corruptions depicted as tasteless, insipid water. The instruction is to instead drink the supreme, deeply flavourful nectar of naam (the divine Name). Vice is flavourless and unsatisfying; only loving remembrance of the Divine offers true, lasting sustenance. The mind must reject the barren forest of maya (worldly attachment) and find its sole nourishment in the elixir of devotion.

Themes: renunciation of vice, naam as spiritual nectar, tastelessness of worldly temptation, soul addressed as companion, drinking divine elixir, abandoning sensual corruption, simran as supreme sustenance
ਕਬੀਰ ਬਿਰਹੁ ਭੁਯੰਗਮੁ ਮਨਿ ਬਸੈ ਮੰਤੁ ਨ ਮਾਨੈ ਕ:
The snake of birha (intense separation from the Divine) has entered and taken residence within the mind after seeking the Guru's sanctuary, and no mantra or exorcism has any power over it. This state of desperate spiritual longing is incurable by ordinary means; the heart seized by yearning for the Beloved cannot be calmed by spells, rituals, or worldly remedies. The imagery declares that true devotion, once awakened through surrender, overwhelms and possesses the consciousness beyond all external control or cure.

Themes: birha, spiritual longing, snake imagery, incurable state, Guru's sanctuary, mantra, yearning for the Divine, possession of the mind
ਹਰਿ ਬਿਨੁ ਕਿਉ ਜੀਵਾ ਮੇਰੀ ਮਾਈ ॥:
The speaker addresses their mother in a rhetorical question that expresses complete existential dependence on the Divine, declaring that life without God is impossible and unbearable. The heart becomes restless and anguished when separated from the divine Name. This is an intimate outpouring of spiritual desperation that frames devotion not as optional practice but as the very condition of survival, positioning the self as incapable of functioning apart from the Beloved's presence.

Themes: separation anxiety, divine dependence, existential desperation, mother as confidant, spiritual restlessness, naam as life-breath, intimate address, rhetorical question as devotion
ਪ੍ਰਭ ਮਿਲਬੇ ਕਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਮਨਿ ਲਾਗੀ ॥:
The soul develops an intense longing to meet the Divine, and deep love for the Creator has awakened within the heart. This is not casual interest but a powerful spiritual awakening that transforms the inner being. The mind now yearns for union with God, having turned away from worldly distractions toward the eternal Beloved. The statement declares that true spiritual journey begins when genuine love for the Divine takes root in consciousness.

Themes: divine love, spiritual longing, union with God, awakening of the heart, yearning for the Beloved, transformation of consciousness, prem (devotional love), man (mind) turning toward the Divine.
ਹਰਿ ਦਰਸਨ ਕਉ ਮੇਰਾ ਮਨੁ ਬਹੁ ਤਪਤੈ ਜਿਉ ਤ੍ਰਿਖਾ:
The seeker's consciousness burns with desperate longing for the divine darshan (sacred sight of the Divine), using the simile of a parched person deprived of water to express the intensity of spiritual thirst. The mind suffers and writhes in separation from the Beloved, unable to find relief through any worldly substitute. This is the voice of viraha, the agony of sacred separation, where love itself becomes a consuming fire that only the Master's presence can extinguish.

Themes: divine darshan, spiritual thirst, viraha (separation), longing of the soul, parched mind, love's burning, sacred vision, desperate yearning.
ਬਾਝਹੁ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਕੋਇ ਨ ਸਾਰੇ ਏਕਲੜੀ ਕੁਰਲਾਏ ॥:
The soul declares absolute dependence on the Divine Beloved: without that bond, no being in the world takes notice or asks after its welfare. Stripped of every companion, the solitary self wails in the wilderness of worldly existence, a concrete image of existential abandonment that reveals the truth that only relationship with the Divine sustains. The crying alone is both literal desolation and the soul's anguished recognition that maya (worldly attachment) offers no real fellowship. This is the voice of separation grief, the pain of viraha, insisting that all other ties are hollow.

Themes: separation from the Divine, wilderness of worldly existence, solitude and abandonment, crying in anguish, no worldly support, dependence on the Beloved, viraha longing, futility of maya
ਮਨਿ ਬੈਰਾਗੁ ਭਇਆ ਦਰਸਨੁ ਦੇਖਣੈ ਕਾ ਚਾਉ ॥:
The mind has grown detached from worldly entanglements and now burns with longing for a glimpse of the Divine. Vairag—spiritual dispassion toward maya (worldly attachment)—has taken root, replaced by an intense yearning for darshan, the blessed sight of the sacred presence. The devotee declares a state of inner transformation: love for the Eternal has awakened, and the heart craves nothing but that vision. Worldly desire has inverted into sacred thirst.

Themes: vairag (detachment), darshan (divine vision), longing, dispassion toward maya, inner transformation, yearning, sacred love, turning away from the world
ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਚਿਰੀ ਵਿਛੁੰਨਿਆ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਬਦਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਪ੍:
A soul long separated from the Divine pleads to be reunited, addressing the Lord as the beloved master and asking Him to come dwell within the heart-home. The Guru's shabad, the sacred word, is the bridge that ends prolonged separation and restores the prodigal to their true abode. Union is not achieved by wandering but through the guidance of revealed sound that leads the wanderer back to inner presence.

Themes: divine union, separation and longing, Guru's shabad as path, heart as true home, return of the soul, beloved Lord, refuge and reunion, inner dwelling
ਪਿਰ ਦੋਸੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਸੁਖਹ ਦਾਤੇ ਹਉ ਵਿਛੁੜੀ ਬੁਰਿਆਰ:
The soul-bride confesses that separation from the Divine Husband arises entirely from her own wrongdoing, absolving the Lord of any blame as the bestower of all peace and comfort. This is an admission of personal accountability, acknowledging that the Giver of sukha (spiritual solace) never withdraws His presence; rather, the individual's own misdeeds create the distance. The statement surrenders self-justification and accepts responsibility for the state of alienation from God.

Themes: divine husband, self-blame, separation caused by sin, acceptance of fault, God as giver of peace, accountability, soul-bride's confession, alienation from the Divine
ਆਉ ਜੀ ਤੂ ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਹਰਿ ਜਸੁ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਸੁਨਾਵਨਾ:
The devotee urgently invites the beloved Guru to enter and abide in the heart's dwelling, making the inner space a sanctuary for divine presence. The request is that the Guru narrate and sing God's praise (kirtan) directly into the ears, enabling the listener to absorb sacred sound through hearing. This expresses deep longing for spiritual instruction, intimate communion, and the transformative experience of receiving wisdom through listening. The plea positions the devotee as receptive, waiting, and dependent on the Guru's arrival to fill inner emptiness with divine resonance.

Themes: invitation, longing, Guru's presence, heart as dwelling, listening to divine praise, kirtan, spiritual intimacy, receptive devotion
ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਰਾਮ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਜੀਉ ॥: A direct, intimate call to the Divine, asking the Beloved to enter and dwell within the heart. The soul addresses the Divine with deep affection and urgency, seeking not distant blessing but immediate, indwelling presence. This is an expression of devotion that frames the heart as a home awaiting its resident, positioning the seeker in a stance of invitation and longing for union with the Divine. Themes: divine intimacy, indwelling presence, heart as sanctuary, loving invocation, soul's longing, devotion, union with the Beloved, invitation to the Divine.
ਬਿਨਵੰਤਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਦਇਆ ਧਾਰਹੁ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਨਾਹ ਪਿਆਰ:
A desperate wife pleads with her divine Husband to shower mercy and return to dwell within her heart. The soul-bride supplicates before her Beloved Lord, begging Him to come abide in her inner chamber. This is the stance of utter dependence and longing: the separated bride cannot live without her Husband's gracious presence, so she entreats Him to pour compassion and make His home in her heart.

Themes: divine Husband, soul-bride's longing, mercy and grace, indwelling Divine, heart as dwelling, supplication, separation and union
ਮੋਹਨ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਕਰਉ ਜੋਦਰੀਆ ॥:
The soul addresses the Divine as the Enchanter and urgently pleads for divine presence to enter and abide within the heart's dwelling. The house is both the physical body and the inner consciousness where the Beloved is invited to take residence. This is a prayer of desperate longing, where the devotee makes entreaties and supplications, seeking union with the Fascinating Lord who captivates the heart. The request reveals the empty home awaiting its true master and the devotee's complete surrender in asking God to dwell within.

Themes: divine indwelling, prayer of longing, heart as sacred dwelling, surrender and supplication, union with the Beloved, God as Enchanter, devotee's entreaty, presence in the heart
ਹਮ ਘਰਿ ਸਾਜਨ ਆਏ ॥:
The Divine, the truest friend and beloved, has arrived and now dwells within the heart's inner home. This is a declaration of realised union: the Lord who was sought outside has manifested within, filling the inner dwelling with divine presence. The soul rejoices that the eternal companion has taken residence in the heart's abode, transforming it into sacred space. The teeka reads "friends" as the singular Lord-Protector who has become manifest within, not merely visiting but abiding.

Themes: divine indwelling, heart as sacred home, Lord as beloved friend, realised union, inner manifestation, soul's joy, presence of the Divine, heart-temple
ਪਹਿਲੈ ਪਹਰੈ ਫੁਲੜਾ ਫਲੁ ਭੀ ਪਛਾ ਰਾਤਿ ॥:
The early phase of spiritual practice yields beauty like blossoms, while the later watches of the night of contemplation bring the fruit of realization. Beginning devotion produces the flower of aspiration; sustained effort over time ripens into the fruit of attainment. The imagery marks a progression: initial stages charm with promise, mature stages deliver concrete spiritual reward. The teeka specifies that the first watch's beauty resembles a flower, whereas fruit comes only at the ambrosial hour.

Themes: stages of spiritual practice, early devotion versus mature realization, flowers as initial promise, fruit as final attainment, progression through night-watches, ambrosial hours of practice, sustained effort bearing results, beauty then substance
ਕਬੀਰ ਸੂਤਾ ਕਿਆ ਕਰਹਿ ਉਠਿ ਕਿ ਨ ਜਪਹਿ ਮੁਰਾਰਿ:
Bhagat Kabir addresses his own soul with urgent admonition, questioning why it remains asleep in the intoxicating sleep of maya (worldly attachment) and wastes this precious human life in vain. The sleep is not physical rest but spiritual negligence, a trance of material delusion. He exhorts the self to awaken, rise, and engage in simran (loving remembrance) of the Divine, rejecting complacency. The call demands immediate action: shake off the slumber of attachment and remember the Lord while there is still time.

Themes: spiritual awakening, admonishing the self, simran, maya as sleep, urgency of human life, divine remembrance, overcoming complacency, self-exhortation
ਪਰਭਾਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਗੁਰ ਕੇ ਚਰਣ ਧਿਆਇ ॥:
The instruction commands the spiritual discipline of rising before dawn to chant the divine Name and fix the mind on the Guru's feet. The feet represent both the physical presence of the teacher and the posture of surrender, humility, and refuge. Simran (loving remembrance) at this hour aligns the consciousness with the Divine, while honouring the Guru who connects the seeker to the Name grounds the practice in devotion and gratitude.

Themes: early morning meditation, divine Name, Guru's feet, surrender and humility, simran, amrit vela, spiritual discipline, refuge.
ਝਾਲਾਘੇ ਉਠਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਨਿਸਿ ਬਾਸੁਰ ਆਰਾਧਿ ॥:
An urgent instruction to the self rises with the pre-dawn hour, commanding the sleeper to wake and immediately take up jap (repetition of the divine Name). The practice begins in the amrit vela (ambrosial hours before dawn) but extends without pause into every moment, making remembrance a continuous discipline rather than a ritual confined to morning. The imperative tone treats spiritual practice as essential and non-negotiable, the first and final duty of human life.

Themes: amrit vela, early rising, naam jap, continuous remembrance, day and night worship, spiritual discipline, daily practice, loving adoration.
ਬਾਬੀਹਾ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਵੇਲੈ ਬੋਲਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਦਰਿ ਸੁਣੀ ਪ:
The rainbird (papiha) cries out in the amrit vela (ambrosial pre-dawn hours), and its call reaches the divine court — its prayer is heard. The bird's desperate longing mirrors the devotee who rises before dawn to seek the Beloved; sincere supplication at that sacred hour never returns empty. Early-morning devotion pierces the highest realm and finds acceptance.

Themes: amrit vela pre-dawn prayer, papiha rainbird longing, divine court acceptance, supplication heard, early-morning devotion, desperate seeking rewarded
ਛਾਤੀ ਸੀਤਲ ਮਨੁ ਸੁਖੀ ਛੰਤ ਗੋਬਿਦ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਇ ॥:
Singing the praises of the Lord of the Universe brings cooling relief to the burning heart and abiding peace to the restless mind. The act of devotional song functions as a remedy, transforming inner turmoil into tranquility. Through glorification of the Divine, the consciousness finds rest and the heart experiences soothing calm, as the pain of separation dissolves in the nectar of praise.

Themes: devotional singing, inner peace, divine praise, cooling of the heart, remedy for suffering, Lord of the Universe, sukh (spiritual comfort), transformation through song
ਜੋਗੁ ਬਨਿਆ ਤੇਰਾ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਈ ॥੧॥:
Singing divine praise becomes the truest form of yogic union — the contemplative discipline ascetics seek is fulfilled not through austere practice but through kirtan, the musical celebration of the Divine. Worldly comfort and the renunciate's contentment both flow from glorifying the Eternal, collapsing the distinction between householder and ascetic. Devotional song replaces formal meditation as the path to absorption in the sacred.

Themes: kirtan as yoga, union through praise, worldly and ascetic joy reconciled, devotional singing, absorption through glorification, householder and renunciate unified, divine praise as spiritual discipline
ਹਉ ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਕਰਉ ॥:
A declaration of unbroken devotion: the speaker commits to continuous kirtan (singing praise) of the divine Name through every moment, night and day. This is not aspiration but settled resolve — a vow of perpetual simran (loving remembrance) that makes glorifying the Divine the sole, unceasing occupation. The stance is one of joyful surrender, anchoring the self in ceaseless praise as life's purpose. The speaker pledges constant recitation and celebration of the sacred Name, making laudation an all-hours practice without pause.

Themes: naam (divine Name), kirtan (singing praise), continuous devotion, simran (loving remembrance), day and night worship, unceasing glorification, joyful surrender, lifelong commitment to praise
ਰੁਣ ਝੁਣੋ ਸਬਦੁ ਅਨਾਹਦੁ ਨਿਤ ਉਠਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਸੰਤਨ ਕ:
The unstruck celestial sound, anahad shabad, resonates as a continuous melodious current of divine praise that must be sung each morning within the company of the holy, the sangat. This primal vibration is the sweet, unbroken music of the Divine's glory, and joining it through daily congregational devotional singing is the prescribed spiritual discipline. The instruction directs the seeker toward collective early-morning worship where the eternal sound-current becomes audible through sustained loving remembrance.

Themes: anahad shabad, unstruck sound current, early morning devotional singing, sangat, divine praise, celestial music, daily spiritual discipline, amrit vela
ਸਾਧੋ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਕੇ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਵਉ ॥:
A direct exhortation addressed to holy seekers and devotees, urging them to continually sing the Glorious Praises of the Lord of the Universe. The instruction is to make kirtan (devotional singing) of the Divine's virtues a constant, unbroken practice — not occasional worship but a sustained remembrance through sacred song. The call goes out to the company of the devout, directing them to keep the divine qualities on their lips without cessation, anchoring awareness in the Eternal Sustainer through continuous vocal praise.

Themes: kirtan of divine virtues, continuous devotional singing, exhortation to holy seekers, praising the Lord of the Universe, sustained remembrance through sacred song, sangat directed to sing God's glories, unbroken practice of divine praise
ਨਿਰਬਾਣ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਵਹੁ ਕਰਤੇ ਕਾ ਨਿਮਖ ਸਿਮਰਤ ਜ:
The instruction commands singing the Creator's praises from a state stripped of desire, because even a moment's simran (loving remembrance) liberates the human being from bondage to vice. The teeka clarifies that nirbanaa signifies freedom from vaasnaa—craving and mental agitation—rather than a metaphysical state alone. Brief contemplation of the divine Name yields release from corruption, establishing that freedom from attachment is both the precondition for true worship and the fruit of even momentary devotion.

Themes: liberation from desire, kirtan (devotional singing), simran (loving remembrance), freedom from vice, momentary meditation, divine Name, detachment, salvation.
ਮਨ ਮੀਠ ਤੁਹਾਰੋ ਕੀਓ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥:
The devotee addresses the Divine with complete surrender, declaring that every divine action is accepted as sweet and pleasing to the mind. This is a stance of total acceptance and contentment, where the soul no longer blames anyone for hardship but embraces the divine will as inherently good. The teeka clarifies that this state arises from having never assigned fault or blame to any being, indicating a consciousness free from grievance and established in trust.

Themes: surrender to divine will, acceptance of pleasure and pain, freedom from blame, contentment, trust in the Creator, sweetness of devotion, equanimity, dissolution of ego-driven complaint.
ਮੀਤ ਕੇ ਕਰਤਬ ਕੁਸਲ ਸਮਾਨਾ ॥੧॥:
Declares complete contentment with the Divine's will, framing the Creator as an intimate Friend whose every deed feels as soothing as comfort itself. The stance is one of joyful surrender and radical acceptance; whatever the Beloved does is experienced not as hardship but as a source of peace. The self finds rest only by aligning its satisfaction with the actions of its Companion, dissolving personal preference into trust.

Themes: divine will, radical acceptance, the Beloved as Friend, surrender, contentment, sukha (comfort), trust in the Creator, dissolving egoic preference
ਸਰਬ ਸੁਖ ਆਨੰਦ ਮੰਗਲ ਰਸ ਮਾਨਿ ਗੋਬਿੰਦੈ ਆਗਿਓ ॥: Accepting the sweet will of the Divine brings total contentment, joy, and auspiciousness. The speaker declares that surrender to God's hukam (divine command) yields all happiness, transforming life into continuous bliss. Rather than seeking peace through worldly means, the devotee finds every pleasure and blessing by embracing divine order with love and trust. This state of acceptance itself becomes the source of lasting fulfillment. Themes: surrender to divine will, contentment through acceptance, hukam as source of joy, mangal as auspicious state, divine order and human happiness, sweet acceptance of God's command, lasting peace through submission.
ਖਿਨ ਮਹਿ ਥਾਪਿ ਉਥਾਪਨਹਾਰਾ ਆਪਨ ਹਾਥਿ ਮਤਾਤ ॥੧॥:
The Divine possesses the power to create and destroy within a single moment, establishing and disestablishing all existence instantaneously. Every decision and outcome remains solely in divine hands; the Creator alone controls all affairs and judgments. No other power can alter what the Divine ordains. This declaration asserts absolute divine sovereignty over the transient world, emphasizing that all authority rests with the One who can raise up or cast down in an instant.

Themes: divine sovereignty, creation and destruction, divine will, transience of worldly power, God's control over fate, impermanence, omnipotence, surrender to divine order.
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਈਐ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੧॥:
The instruction commands constant loving remembrance of the divine Name as the means to bring all worldly tasks and spiritual concerns to successful completion. Remembering God settles affairs, fulfills objectives, and resolves difficulties that otherwise remain unfinished. The teaching promises that embedding the divine presence in the mind through simran (loving remembrance) ensures that every endeavor reaches its proper end and purpose is accomplished.

Themes: naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), success and fulfillment, divine assistance, problem resolution, purpose of life, trust in God, spiritual practice.
ਕਾਰਜੁ ਤੇਰਾ ਹੋਵੈ ਪੂਰਾ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਇ:
A direct instruction to the self to continually sing the attributes of the Divine, given as the certain method by which all personal affairs and life's central purpose reach successful fulfillment. The counsel promises that remembrance through song guarantees that one's efforts bear fruit, linking the resolution of worldly tasks to the spiritual act of praising the Creator.

Themes: divine praise, fulfillment of affairs, instructing the mind, singing God's virtues, remembrance, success through devotion, surrender to divine will, purpose of life.
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਅਰਾਧਣਾ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੮॥:
Loving remembrance of the divine Name is the sole worthwhile capital of human life; through that remembrance all worldly and spiritual affairs reach successful completion. The central instruction is to make naam (the divine Name) one's stock-in-trade, for simran (loving remembrance) fulfils every purpose and resolves every undertaking. Devotional worship of the Lord is the one investment whose return is the fruition of all life's goals.

Themes: naam simran, divine Name as capital, fulfilment of life's purpose, resolution of affairs, devotional worship, spiritual investment, success through remembrance, surrender to the Lord
ਸਭੇ ਕਾਜ ਸਵਾਰਿਐ ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੰਦਾ ॥੭॥:
All tasks and affairs are set right and fulfilled when the Divine is pleased and accepts the devotee. Divine favor and the alignment of human will with divine will (raza) are the sole cause of worldly success and spiritual resolution; without that acceptance, effort is fruitless. The resolution of every worldly and spiritual undertaking depends entirely on earning God's pleasure and grace.

Themes: divine pleasure, resolution of affairs, raza (divine will), God's grace, fulfillment of tasks, dependence on the Divine, spiritual acceptance
ਸਗਲ ਮਨੋਰਥ ਪੂਰਨ ਹੋਏ ਕਦੇ ਨ ਹੋਇ ਦੁਖਾਲਾ ਜੀਉ:
The speaker declares that all aspirations and heart's desires have been fully satisfied through union with the Divine, resulting in a permanent state free from suffering and sorrow. Where worldly hopes remain unfulfilled and lead to anguish, the devotee who has attained the divine presence experiences complete fulfillment that never fades. The pain of lack and longing is permanently extinguished, never to return, because the ultimate aim of human life has been reached.

Themes: fulfillment of desires, end of suffering, divine grace, contentment, liberation from sorrow, answered prayers, spiritual completion, removal of pain
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਆਧਾਰੁ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਆਸਰਾ ॥:
The lotus feet of the Divine are the sole foundation and refuge for devotees, the complete support upon which life depends. This is a declaration of absolute dependence and surrender, where the servant finds safety and stability only at the feet of the Master. The image of the lotus foot conveys beauty, purity, and the destination of loving devotion, while the assertion of dependence affirms that the bhagat (devotee) has no other shelter or hope.

Themes: lotus feet, refuge and surrender, divine support, dependence on the Master, bhagat (devotee), shelter, foundation, protection.
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸੇਵੀ ਰਿਦ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਗੁਰ ਪੂਰੇ ਕੈ ਆਧਾਰਿ:
The seeker takes refuge in the perfect Guru and fixes the mind's attention on the Lord's beautiful feet, holding that focus steady within the heart. The lotus feet image evokes both the radiant presence of the Divine and the posture of surrender and protection. Internal worship means keeping divine remembrance anchored in consciousness rather than performing external rituals. Reliance on the Guru provides the foundation and support necessary to maintain this inner focus.

Themes: lotus feet, inner devotion, Guru's refuge, surrender, heart-centered worship, divine remembrance, spiritual support, meditation.
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸਿਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਰੀਤਿ ਸੰਤਨ ਮਨਿ ਆਵਏ ਜੀਉ:
The saints enshrine within their hearts the discipline and way of life centered on loving the beautiful lotus feet of the Supreme Being. This love for the divine presence becomes the guiding principle and established order that occupies the mind of the devout. The lotus feet represent both the image of the Divine presence and the stance of taking refuge and surrender. Only the company of the truly devoted holds this path of loving attachment to the divine Name.

Themes: lotus feet, loving devotion, saints' discipline, refuge and surrender, divine presence, heart's occupation, way of life, sangat.
ਬੋਹਿਥੜਾ ਹਰਿ ਚਰਣ ਮਨ ਚੜਿ ਲੰਘੀਐ ॥:
The Divine's lotus feet function as a sturdy vessel; boarding this sacred craft ferries the soul across the ocean of worldly existence. The mind is addressed directly and urged to embark upon the Lord's feet as one's ship of deliverance, the reliable ferry that carries consciousness past the terrifying sea of samsara. Taking refuge at the divine feet is the means of crossing over, transcending maya (worldly attachment) by mounting the raft of God's presence rather than drowning in material delusion.

Themes: lotus feet as boat, ocean of existence, crossing over, divine refuge, mind's instruction, samsara, surrender, deliverance
ਹਰਿ ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਮਨੁ ਬੇਧਿਆ ਕਿਛੁ ਆਨ ਨ ਮੀਠਾ ਰਾਮ:
The mind pierced by the Lord's lotus feet finds no other sweetness appealing, declaring complete spiritual saturation where divine refuge alone satisfies. The image of piercing suggests irreversible attachment—the heart, once transfixed by the beauty of the divine presence, loses all taste for worldly attractions. The sovereign Lord becomes the sole source of delight, rendering all other experiences bland by comparison. This is a statement of exclusive devotion born from deep inner transformation.

Themes: lotus feet, divine refuge, piercing attachment, exclusive devotion, spiritual satisfaction, loss of worldly taste, surrender, transformation of heart
ਪੀ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਆਘਾਨਿਆ ਗੁਰਿ ਅਮਰੁ ਕਰਾਇਆ ॥੨॥:
The devotee drinks the ambrosial nectar of the divine Name and reaches total inner satisfaction; through the Guru's intervention this nectar confers deathlessness—a state beyond aging, beyond mortality, beyond all sorrow's reach. The Guru transforms the seeker into one who has conquered time itself. Spiritual immortality here means no second birth, no decline, no touch of grief ever again. The teeka stresses that this exalted spiritual state never ages and death never approaches it.

Themes: amrit (ambrosial nectar), immortality through Guru, deathlessness, freedom from sorrow, naam as nectar, spiritual transformation, conquest of time, inner satisfaction
ਜਿਨ੍ਹ ਪੀਆ ਸੇ ਮਸਤ ਭਏ ਹੈ ਤੂਟੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਫਾਹੇ ॥:
Those who drink the nectar of naam (the divine Name) become spiritually intoxicated, lost in divine bliss, and all their worldly attachments and fetters of maya (worldly attachment) are permanently severed. The image of drinking represents internalising divine love, while intoxication signals a state beyond rational control, wholly absorbed in the Beloved. The breaking of bonds and snares signifies liberation from the entanglements of worldly existence, the cycle of birth and death, and the ego's grip. The transformation is total: bondage gives way to freedom through the taste of divine essence.

Themes: spiritual intoxication, liberation from maya, divine nectar, breaking of bonds, naam simran (loving remembrance), freedom from attachment, transformation through devotion, severing worldly fetters.
ਹਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਸੋ ਚਖੈ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨਾ ॥੨॥:
The soul that drinks the immortal nectar of the divine Name receives spiritual life, addressing the self as witness to this transformative consumption. Amrit (immortal nectar) represents the essence of the Divine that ends the thirst of repeated births. The teeka emphasizes that this drinking of Harinam (the Lord's Name) bestows atma (soul) life, moving beyond mere taste to full absorption. The instruction urges the mind toward this essential sustenance.

Themes: amrit, Harinam, spiritual nourishment, immortal nectar, soul's thirst, divine Name, inner awakening, addressing the mind.
ਗੁਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਚੋਇਆ ਮੇਰੀ ਜਿੰਦੁੜੀ:
The Guru pours the life-giving nectar of the divine Name into the mouth, reviving a soul that had perished from spiritual death. This act of grace restores the dead to life, transforming one who was dying from separation into one who now lives through connection. The image of pouring nectar directly into the mouth conveys intimate initiation and the bestowal of amrit (immortal nectar) that alone can overcome the death of the ego-self.

Themes: spiritual revival, Guru's grace, amrit (divine nectar), naam (divine Name), resurrection from spiritual death, initiation, restoration of the soul, life through devotion
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਮਿਲਿ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥:
The divine Name (naam) is declared a treasure-house of amrit, the deathless nectar that confers immortality. The instruction is communal: seekers must join together in sangat (holy fellowship) to drink this essence, emphasizing that spiritual nourishment is found collectively rather than in isolation. The exhortation positions remembrance of the Divine as both the supreme wealth and the sustaining elixir, urging brothers of destiny to partake through shared practice.

Themes: naam as amrit, spiritual treasure, communal drinking, sangat, divine nectar, collective remembrance, immortality, fellowship of seekers.
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟਿਓਨੁ ਫਿਰਿ ਜੋਨਿ ਨ ਪਾਏ ॥:
The Divine eliminates the devotee's terror of repeated birth and death, granting permanent release from the cycle of transmigration. Through divine grace the soul escapes rebirth entirely — no longer cast again into worldly existence, no longer subjected to the revolving wheel of coming and going. Liberation here means the cessation of return: the fear of dying and being born is severed at its root, and the being is never again plunged into the round of species and wombs.

Themes: liberation from transmigration, ending the cycle of birth and death, fear of reincarnation removed, permanent release from rebirth, divine grace granting mukti, escape from the wheel of existence, freedom from coming and going
ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਮ ਕਾ ਭਉ ਲਥਾ ॥੨੦॥:
Inner stability arises, the Divine is encountered, and the terror of death falls away. The speaker declares that when the mind attains equipoise—sahaj, the state of natural balance—union with God follows automatically. This spiritual realization dissolves the fear of Yama, the messenger of death, because the devotee has transcended the domain where death holds power. The causal sequence is explicit: mental stillness enables divine discovery, which in turn liberates one from existential dread and the fear of postmortem judgment.

Themes: sahaj (spiritual poise), finding God, freedom from fear of death, Yama, inner stability, liberation from dread, divine union, overcoming mortality.
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਜਪਿ ॥:
The fear of birth and death—the terror of the entire cycle of coming and going—is severed when the devotee dwells in the company of the devout (sangat) and recites the hymns of praise. The teeka reads "janam maran" not merely as literal reincarnation but as the dread pervading one's whole mortal span, a lifelong anxiety dissolved through gurbani. Meditation on the divine Word as received through the Guru's servant becomes the sole means of liberation from existential fear, cutting the bondage of transmigration.

Themes: fear of death and rebirth, shabad (divine Word) as liberation, sangat (company of the devout), cycle of transmigration, existential dread dissolved, recitation of praise, servanthood, bondage severed
ਨ ਦਨੋਤਿ ਜਸਮਰਣੇਨ ਜਨਮ ਜਰਾਧਿ ਮਰਣ ਭਇਅੰ ॥੧॥ ਰ:
Loving remembrance of the Divine dissolves the terror of repeated birth, aging, and death. Through simran (loving remembrance), the cycle of transmigration loses its grip; anxiety, worldly worry, and mortality's dread simply cease to touch the devotee. The practice of holding the divine Name in consciousness severs the root of existential fear, granting freedom from the suffering inherent in embodied existence across lifetimes.

Themes: simran conquering fear of death, liberation from transmigration cycle, naam erasing existential anxiety, freedom from old age and rebirth, meditation dissolving mortality's dread, overcoming worldly worry through remembrance
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਦੁਖੁ ਕਾਟੀਐ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਚੂਕੈ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਕਾਣੇ:
Loving devotion to the Beloved Divine severs the entire cycle of birth and death, ending all suffering accumulated across lifetimes. The terror of the Messenger of Death dissolves permanently. Through the company of the devout (sangat), the accumulated distress of one's whole existence is cut away, and the dread of death's emissary is extinguished. Bondage to transmigration is broken; fear of the afterlife's judge vanishes.

Themes: liberation from transmigration, ending the cycle of rebirth and death, fear of the Messenger of Death destroyed, suffering eradicated through devotion, sangat as the context of liberation, divine love as the means of release, death's fear overcome
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭੈ ਲਾਥੇ ॥੪॥੨॥੫੨॥:
The speaker declares that all fear surrounding the cycle of birth and death has been removed, indicating a state of spiritual liberation attained through connection with the Divine. The terror of transmigration, the anxiety of repeated incarnations, and the dread of mortality no longer bind the devotee who has found refuge in the holy presence. This is a statement of attained freedom rather than a plea or aspiration, marking the culmination of faithful practice and surrender.

Themes: liberation from birth-death cycle, freedom from fear, overcoming mortality, spiritual emancipation, end of transmigration, release from anxiety, devotee's attained state, surrender to the Divine
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੈ ਆਸਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਿਉ ਰੰਗੁ ਲਾਏ ॥:
Taking refuge in sangat (the company of the devout) kindles deep love for the Divine. The fellowship of holy seekers becomes the shelter through which the soul attaches to the Creator with devotion. Sacred companionship anchors the mind in longing for the Divine, turning it toward union with the Supreme. The teeka confirms this straightforwardly: dwelling in the support of spiritual company, one falls in love with the Supreme Being.

Themes: sangat, divine love, refuge, attachment to the Creator, spiritual companionship, devotion, shelter of holy company
ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗਿ ਤਰੀਜੈ ਸਾਗਰੁ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਫਾਸਾ ਜੀ:
The company of the holy, sangat, enables the soul to cross the world-ocean, the vast expanse of worldly existence and maya that separates the individual from the Divine. Through this sacred association, the noose of death, the binding rope of the divine messenger that ensnares souls in the cycle of rebirth, is severed and rendered powerless. Liberation from the cycle of transmigration becomes possible only through collective spiritual practice, not solitary effort.

Themes: sangat (holy company), world-ocean, liberation from rebirth, severing death's noose, cycle of transmigration, spiritual fellowship, divine messenger, freedom from bondage.
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੀ ਭੀਰ ਜਉ ਪਾਈ ਤਉ ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਸੰਗਿ:
Entering the assembly of the devout, the sangat (company of the devout), becomes the direct path to union with the Divine. Immersion in holy fellowship dissolves separation from the Creator; the seeker who finds such sacred company attains the Lord's presence. Communion with saintly souls yields the meeting with the eternal Beloved, transforming isolation into divine intimacy.

Themes: sangat (company of the devout), union with the Divine, holy fellowship, meeting the Lord, sacred assembly, divine intimacy, removal of separation, spiritual companionship
ਸੰਤਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਸੰਗ ਸੁਰੰਗ ਰਤੇ ਜਸੁ ਗਾਵਤ ਹ:
The holy ones dwell perpetually absorbed in sangat (the company of the devout), remaining immersed in this spiritual fellowship. Colored by a beautiful, pure love—the celestial hue of devotion—they sing divine praise, celebrating the glory of the One. The image of being dyed in a color signifies total saturation and transformation of the self through loving remembrance, where the devotee becomes the praise they offer.

Themes: sangat, divine praise, spiritual absorption, transformation through love, devotional coloring, holy company, saturation in devotion, celebration of the Divine
ਕਾਢਿ ਲੀਏ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਆਨ ਬਿਖੈ ਤੇ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਮਨੁ ਲਾਵ:
A direct plea to the Divine to rescue the human mind from entanglement in worldly vices and sensual attachments. The prayer asks for extraction from countless corrupting influences and subsequent connection to the company of the holy, where the mind finds its true anchoring. God is addressed as the sole agent capable of pulling consciousness out of maya (worldly illusion) and securing it within the sangat (congregation of the devout).

Themes: divine rescue, detachment from vice, attachment to holy company, prayer for liberation, refuge in the congregation, grace as the means of extraction, mind as the site of struggle.
ਮਹਿਮਾ ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗ ਕੀ ਸੁਨਹੁ ਮੇਰੇ ਮੀਤਾ ॥:
Declares the supreme greatness of sangat (the company of the devout) and urges companions to attend to this truth. The gathering of seekers under the Guru's shelter possesses unmatched glory, and one should listen closely to this declaration of its power. Fellowship with the holy congregation is elevated as the highest good, a collective refuge worth heeding.

Themes: sangat (holy congregation), glory of sacred fellowship, listening to wisdom, companionship on the spiritual path, Guru's shelter, devotees' gathering, heed the teaching
ਮੇਰਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ ਸੁਖਦਾਈ ॥:
The speaker declares that their Guru is the form of the Supreme Lord, the one who grants all peace and comfort. This is a statement of personal conviction and intimate relationship, identifying the spiritual guide with the Divine itself. The Guru is not merely a teacher but the bestower of tranquility, the source of all solace, and the embodiment of the transcendent God who gives rest to the soul.

Themes: Guru as Divine, peace-giver, personal relationship with the Divine, Guru as God's form, solace and comfort, Supreme Lord, intimate devotion, spiritual refuge
ਤੁਮ ਦਾਤੇ ਤੁਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਬਿਧਾਤੇ ॥:
The speaker addresses the Divine directly, acknowledging God as the sole source of all creation and the bestower of every gift. The teeka clarifies that the Divine not only gives but pervades all beings as the immanent presence. This is an affirmation of complete dependence: the Creator alone originates life, sustains existence, and grants all provisions. The stance is one of humble recognition, stripping away any sense of human agency in giving or creating.

Themes: divine creator, bestower of gifts, immanent presence, source of all life, dependence on God, recognition of the giver, pervading all beings, singular agency.
ਕਰੁਣਾ ਮੈ ਕਿਰਪਾਲ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਨਿਧਿ ਜੀਵਨ ਪਦ ਨਾਨਕ:
The speaker addresses the Divine as the very source and embodiment of mercy, the treasure-house of compassion, and the master of grace—then pleads for the gift of sacred vision. Darshan, the blessed sight of the Divine presence, is not mere seeing but the bestower of the highest spiritual status, granting the state of jeevan pad, the redeemed life lived in conscious union with the Divine while still in the body. The plea arises from a recognition of the Divine as inherently compassionate, the sole giver of the exalted state that transcends ordinary existence.

Themes: divine mercy, compassion, darshan, jeevan pad, spiritual liberation, grace, pleading prayer, sacred vision.
ਤੂੰ ਭਾਰੋ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਗੁਣੀ ਗਹੇਰਾ ॥੨॥:
Declares the Divine as the ultimate sovereign master and an unfathomable reservoir of virtuous qualities. Acknowledges the Creator's profound depth and limitless excellence, establishing a stance of humble devotion and absolute reliance on that boundless spiritual wealth. The Divine is both the supreme authority to be surrendered to and the deep ocean of merit to be sought.

Themes: divine sovereignty, boundless virtue, spiritual treasure, surrender, unfathomable depth, reliance on the Creator, ocean of merit
ਦੇਵਣਹਾਰੁ ਦਾਤਾਰੁ ਕਿਤੁ ਮੁਖਿ ਸਾਲਾਹੀਐ ॥:
The Divine is the supreme giver who bestows sustenance upon all beings, yet no created mouth can adequately praise such boundless generosity. The rhetorical question exposes the inadequacy of human speech to fully glorify the One whose gifts are beyond measure. Any attempt at praise falls short because the Creator's giving nature exceeds what any creature's words can capture, leaving the devotee in speechless humility before overwhelming grace.

Themes: divine generosity, inadequacy of praise, limits of human speech, rhetorical humility, Creator as sustainer, boundless giving, devotional speechlessness, gratitude beyond words
ਤੇਰੇ ਕਵਨ ਕਵਨ ਗੁਣ ਕਹਿ ਕਹਿ ਗਾਵਾ ਤੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਗ:
The devotee asks which virtues to sing and proclaim, overwhelmed by the infinite qualities of the Divine, who is the master and the treasure-house of all excellence. The rhetorical question confesses the impossibility of fully enumerating divine attributes, praising the Lord as the source and storehouse of every merit. The speaker offers reverent homage while acknowledging human limitation before divine fullness.

Themes: divine virtues, praise and kirtan, God as treasure, devotion, inadequacy of speech, surrender, rhetorical questioning, divine attributes.
ਰੇ ਬਉਰੇ ਤੁਹਿ ਘਰੀ ਨ ਰਾਖੈ ਕੋਈ ॥:
An admonition addressed to the wandering, foolish mind warns that no one will offer shelter even for a single ghari, a brief moment. The mind that strays from the Divine will find itself utterly abandoned, with no refuge in any household. The warning exposes the consequence of spiritual madness: total rejection, homelessness, and the denial of lasting sanctuary from all worldly relations.

Themes: admonition of the mind, spiritual madness, abandonment, rejection, homelessness, impermanence of worldly shelter, consequence of wandering, warning.
ਕਾਹੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਡੋਲਤਾ ਹਰਿ ਮਨਸਾ ਪੂਰਣਹਾਰੁ ॥:
The speaker admonishes his own wavering mind, asking why it continues to sway in doubt and restlessness when the Divine stands ready to fulfill all hopes and heart's desires. The question implies that anxiety is unnecessary—the Lord completes what is lacking, satisfying the soul's deepest longings. Rather than pleading, the stance is corrective: stop your instability, recognize that the Fulfiller already exists, and abandon the impulse to seek elsewhere. Trust in divine sufficiency replaces mental agitation.

Themes: self-admonition, wavering mind, divine fulfiller of desires, trust versus doubt, inner stability, heart's longings, recognition of God's sufficiency, abandoning anxiety.
ਰੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਭੀ ਭਜੁ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ॥੨॥:
An urgent self-admonition commanding the mind to pursue the Lord of the Universe. The speaker exhorts their own consciousness to abandon its current attachments and engage in the worship of the Supreme Being. The word "too" implies that others have already found refuge in the Divine, and the mind must not lag behind in spiritual neglect. It insists on active, deliberate meditation and loving remembrance as the mind's essential duty and ultimate shelter.

Themes: self-admonition, simran (loving remembrance), Gobind (Lord of the Universe), spiritual urgency, duty of the mind, divine refuge, meditation, abandoning neglect
ਮਨ ਮੇਰਿਆ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਤੇਰੈ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਵਸਤੁ:
The speaker addresses his own mind with urgent instruction, revealing that the supreme treasure—the Divine, source of all peace—already dwells within the self. The mind is admonished to abandon its futile search in external places, forests, and worldly objects for what is ever-present internally. True wealth lies not in outward wandering but in recognizing the indwelling Lord, the reservoir of joy accessible through inner awareness rather than external seeking.

Themes: antar, inner dwelling, divine treasure within, self-instruction, futility of external seeking, indwelling Lord, true wealth, turning inward
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਤੂ ਕਾਏ ਦੇਖਿ ਭੁਲਾਨਾ ॥:
Direct admonition of one's own mind for losing its way after beholding maya (worldly attachment). The mind is addressed as a madman, bewildered and straying from the path of righteous living by becoming infatuated with perishable worldly spectacle. This is self-instruction urging the wandering consciousness to listen, wake from delusion, and stop drifting astray through fascination with transitory illusion.

Themes: admonishing the mind, maya as delusion, wandering astray, spiritual awakening, self-correction, infatuation with the perishable, call to listen, lost path
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਥੀਉ ਰੇਣੁ ਜਿਨੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਧਿਆਇਆ ॥:
Direct instruction to the wandering mind: abandon pride and become the dust beneath the feet of those who hold the Divine in remembrance. The counsel addresses the mind as deluded and restless, prescribing radical self-abasement as the path to union with the Lord. Only by surrendering ego and taking the lowest place before the devout can the seeker attain the divine meeting. Falling at the feet of those absorbed in simran (loving remembrance) is the prescribed discipline for attaining God.

Themes: humility, dust of the saints' feet, simran, ego-surrender, sangat, divine union, self-abasement, admonishing the mind
ਲਖ ਖੁਸੀਆ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹੀਆ ਜੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇਇ:
A single merciful glance from the satguru (the true Guru) yields joy equivalent to hundreds of thousands of imperial reigns. The seeker experiences a contentment that surpasses all worldly sovereignty, obtained not through personal effort but through the Guru's sovereign grace. That one look carries more spiritual wealth than countless kingdoms, transforming the devotee's inner state into one of supreme fulfillment and royal abundance.

Themes: satguru's grace, glace of compassion, spiritual contentment versus worldly power, divine favor, inner sovereignty, joy of devotion, kingdom of the mind, grace as unearned gift
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ ਤਾ ਦੁਖੁ ਨ ਜਾਣੀਐ ॥:
Declares that when the True Guru shows compassion, suffering ceases to register as suffering. The pain may still arise but the devotee no longer perceives it as distress, for the Guru's grace transforms the inner response. This is not mere relief but a fundamental shift in how hardship is experienced—the affliction loses its sting. The merciful Guru grants a state in which worldly trouble cannot touch the core of the being.

Themes: Guru's grace, end of suffering, transformed perception, compassion, relief from distress, inner peace, devotee's protection, spiritual solace
ਹਰਿ ਚਉਥੜੀ ਲਾਵ ਮਨਿ ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਇਆ ਬਲਿ:
The fourth round of the marriage ceremony marks the culmination of spiritual union, where the soul-bride attains sahaj (natural equipoise) and discovers the Divine presence. This final stage represents complete absorption in the Lord, producing unshakable inner stability and peace. The mind that wandered in earlier stages now rests in natural balance, having found its eternal companion. The speaker declares total surrender and gratitude, offering themselves in sacrifice to the beloved Ram.

Themes: fourth round, spiritual marriage, sahaj equipoise, divine union, inner peace, soul-bride, surrender, attainment of the Lord
ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਨਾਇ ॥:
The seeker attains lasting comfort and fulfilment by enshrining the True Guru within the heart and living in a way that pleases that inner presence. All desired fruits are secured through this act of inner installation and devotional alignment. Surrender to the spiritual preceptor's wisdom is the direct means by which tranquillity is realised and the restless mind finds its rest.

Themes: true Guru, inner peace, pleasing the Guru, enshrining the Guru in the heart, attaining desired fruits, surrender to the preceptor, spiritual comfort, devotion yielding fulfilment
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਮੇਰਾ ਸਦਾ ਸਹਾਈ ਜਿਨਿ ਦੁਖ ਕਾ ਕਾਟਿਆ:
The true Guru is an everlasting helper and protector who severs suffering at its root for every person who takes his shelter. He dismantles the very banner of pain, uprooting affliction entirely rather than merely easing it. The one who eradicates the deep-seated thorn of sorrow becomes a constant support, a perpetual refuge for the seeker. This is a declaration of unwavering trust in the Guru as the permanent destroyer of distress and the eternal ally of those who surrender.

Themes: satguru as eternal helper, removal of suffering at its root, refuge and surrender to the Guru, destruction of pain's banner, constant divine support, eradication of sorrow's foundation
ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਮਿਲਣ ਕੀ ਇਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਬਰੀਆ ॥:
The line declares that human life presents a singular, unrepeatable opportunity to attain union with the Divine, the Lord of the Universe. It frames this moment as a rare opening, a designated time to bridge the separation between the soul and its Source. The statement urges immediate recognition and action, warning that this chance to meet the Beloved must not be wasted.

Themes: divine union, opportunity of human life, urgency, meeting the Lord, soul's purpose, rare chance, Govind, spiritual timing
ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀ ਤੂੰ ਆਇਆ ਲਾਹਾ ਲੈਣਿ ॥:
The speaker addresses the human soul directly, declaring that birth into this world carries a specific purpose: to earn spiritual profit. The merchant imagery frames life as a trading journey where one must gather the wealth of naam (the divine Name) before departing. Human existence is not accidental but an opportunity for gathering what endures. The line instructs and reminds the listener that this precious human birth was given specifically to accumulate spiritual earnings, not worldly goods.

Themes: human birth as opportunity, spiritual profit, naam as wealth, purpose of life, merchant metaphor, divine remembrance, soul's journey, earning what endures.
ਹਰਿ ਭਗਤਿ ਦ੍ਰਿੜੁ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਾਧ ਨਾਨਕ ਤੇਰੈ ਕਾਮਿ:
The company of the holy (sangat) plants devotion to the Divine firmly within the heart, making loving worship an inseparable part of one's inner being. This sacred association is the sole action that will ultimately serve the soul, the only deed of genuine consequence. Meeting true devotees roots bhagati (devotional worship) so deeply that remembrance of the Lord becomes the heart's permanent disposition rather than a passing act. The teeka specifies that this inner implantation of devotion through holy company is the one deed that accompanies the soul as its true asset.

Themes: sangat (holy company), bhagati (devotional worship) planted in heart, sole worthwhile action, inner transformation through sacred association, devotion as permanent disposition, what truly accompanies the soul, meeting sadhus (the devout)
ਜੀਵਨਾ ਸਫਲ ਜੀਵਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਪਿ ਜਪਿ ਸਦ ਜੀਵਨਾ:
Human life achieves its ultimate purpose and becomes successful only through hearing of the Divine and perpetually engaging in simran (loving remembrance). Such a person transcends mortality and lives eternally. The declaration establishes that listening to spiritual truth and repeating the divine Name are the sole criteria for a fulfilled, victorious existence; without this practice, life remains incomplete and fleeting.

Themes: purposeful existence, simran (loving remembrance), hearing the divine Name, eternal life, spiritual success, fulfilled human birth
